LEARNING PATH LESSON · FEELINGS & KINDNESS · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Welcome, Belong, Trust & Connect — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson begins the graduation: four words about WE — the open door, the fixed spot, the kept promise and the thread that runs underneath every one of them.

What is this?

Welcome opens the door, belong finds the seat that is yours, trust keeps the promises that hold, and connect is the checking-in thread that runs underneath all three.

What does it mean?

Belonging is not a mood that appears — it is built out of small fixed things: a coat hook with a name, a cup that is always theirs, a goodbye that always comes with a return. Children who can NAME their belonging carry it anywhere.

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs three ideas: welcome is a door you can HOLD for others now (you know how it feels to be welcomed — pass it on); belong is made of EVIDENCE (hooks, cups, seats, songs — pointable things); and trust is kept promises, small ones most of all.

Why this matters

The class closes its circle here: the feelings words named the inside, the kindness words aimed outward — and the belonging words name the WE that holds it all. Everything after this card is harvest.

What it teaches

Sense of belonging (the strongest single protective factor in child development research), trust-building through reliability, family identity (the we), and welcoming agency — the child as door-holder for others.

Words to learn

welcomebelongtrustconnectfamilypromisemy spot

Say this to your child

“"Four words hold our family up. Welcome — you are wanted here, always; the door is not locked to you, not ever. Belong — this is your hook, your cup, your seat, your bedtime song; you are not a guest here, you are a beam in the house. Trust — I keep my word to you, small word, small promises especially: the sticker saved, the park kept, the return on time. And connect — we check in, we laugh at the same silly thing, we are us. Four beams. And you — you get to hold the door for others now, because you know exactly how it feels from the inside."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "The four WE words."
  2. Read the panels: the waving girl WELCOMEs, the content boy BELONGs, the hand-on-heart girl TRUSTs, the open-armed boy CONNECTs.
  3. Run the belonging hunt below — find the child’s name (literally or figuratively) all over the house.
  4. Make one small trust-promise today and keep it visibly: "I said I would save you the sticker — here it is." Trust is built at sticker scale.
  5. Close with the takeaway: "welcome, belong, trust, connect — four beams, one house, and you live in it."

Look closer at the picture

On this card four panels hold the WE: Welcome, a waving girl; Belong, a content boy with hands clasped; Trust, a girl with a hand on her heart; and Connect, a boy reaching out with open arms — the family’s beams, drawn warmly.

Ask your child

"Where is your spot in this house?" "What is a promise kept this week?" "What does connect look like in our family?" "Who could WE welcome this week?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say: "That is MY hook!" "you kept your promise!" (trust, noticed) or the pass-it-on: "can my friend come in? I will hold the door."

Out in the real world

Belonging evidence fills the house: the toothbrush with the favourite colour, the drawing taped at child height, the same three books at bedtime, the seat that is always theirs in the car. Point at them occasionally — "yours, yours, yours" — and the abstract word becomes a house tour.

Try it together

The Belonging Hunt: walk the house with a detective’s eye and find ten pieces of belonging evidence — the hook, the cup, the shoe spot, the bedtime song, the drawing on the wall, the family photo, the garden patch, the car seat, the snack shelf, the always-yours chair. Photograph or draw the best ones into a little book titled WHERE I BELONG. Belonging, once you hunt it, turns out to have been everywhere.

Understanding check

Ask: "Which word means the seat is yours? What is trust made of? Who holds the door now?" Belong, kept promises, you do — three answers and the house stands.

Parent tips

Build trust at the smallest scale — children audit promises at four with forensic seriousness, so promise LESS and keep MORE; a kept sticker-promise outweighs a hundred lectures on reliability. And when the family welcomes a guest, hand your child the door: the welcomed child who becomes the welcomer has completed the entire lesson without noticing it was a lesson.

This lesson pairs with the Welcome, Belong, Trust & Connect flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Feelings & Kindness (Class 38).
